title.analysis: Authentic title "1000s Are About to Get Rich Off SpaceX. Could You?" promises an insider-wealth explanation plus a personal-access answer. The script delivers both (employees, funds, Founders Fund, Alphabet; four retail routes) and a strong valuation caution. Accurate in frame; several return multiples quoted along the way are internally inconsistent.

script.stored_text_completeness: All 46045 canonical characters read sequentially in full in 1 bounded ranges; auto-generated untimed text; stored text is about 8,300 words for a 50.4-minute video and ends on the sign-off ("Thanks for watching and I'll see you in the next one."); one "[snorts]" tag; ticker rendered both "SPCX" and "SPC-X"; "Hi V like" for Hiive; audio, timed delivery and editing unverified.
script.opening_words: 13,000 people are about to wake up rich. Not lottery rich, generational rich, the kind of rich where your grandkids are still living off a decision you made years ago by taking a job at a rocket company and getting paid partly in something most people would have thrown in a drawer and forgotten about. In a few days, that drawer turns into a Nasdaq ticker and the single biggest IPO in the history of the planet goes live. 13,000
script.ending_words: curious. Drop a comment and tell me which of the four routes you'd actually take. Are you requesting shares at the IPO price, waiting for the dust to settle and the lockup to hit, going the boring Alphabet route, or just watching the whole circus from the couch with a bowl of cereal? No wrong answers. I read these. Thanks for watching and I'll see you in the next one.
script.analysis: Full 46045 canonical characters read. A 50-minute single-narrator explainer: hook on 13,000 insiders, IPO facts (SPCX, $135, $1.75T, 30% retail), record size vs Aramco, valuation ladder, employee tenders, executive stakes, Founders Fund and Alphabet returns, how IPOs work (S-1, roadshow, allocation, Ritter pops, lockups), IPO history (Google, Amazon, Tesla, Facebook, Airbnb), bull case (launch share, Starlink economics, moat, Starship, defense, ARK), control and pay package, four retail routes (IPO allocation, open market, accredited secondaries, Alphabet and funds incl. DXYZ premium), bear case (revenue multiple, GAAP loss, Morningstar $780B, IPO underperformance), practical rules (wait, size at 1%, DCA, scams), objections, close. Facts are largely consistent with later coverage; return multiples (62,000%, 64x, 100x revenue) do not follow from the script's own inputs.
